text:
fran: Heads-up — discovered a nasty onboarding/security edge: an example Docker image accidentally had ~/.redwood/session.json baked into the image, so when we scaled the container the session belonged to the wrong org and requests were billed there.

sam: whoa. how did a session file end up in the image?

fran: dev had run `redwood login` inside the container during dev and then `docker commit` the container for a demo. image pushed to internal registry. anyone who ran the image got the embedded session.

aditya: reproduction steps (local):
```
# build image with session present
docker build -t redwood-demo .
docker run -e PORT=8080 redwood-demo # app uses baked session
# requests go to baked-session org
```

fran: impact: low billing, but big trust issue — environment leakage across demos / k8s rollouts. could also leak project-scoped keys.

ci-bot: opened RW-9998 "docker-image-baked-session-leak" (assignee: sam)

sam: immediate mitigations: 1) invalidate sessions on startup if running in container (check for DOCKER_* or /.dockerenv) and warn; 2) add an ENTRYPOINT check in official sample Dockerfile that removes ~/.redwood/session.json at startup; 3) docs note: never commit session files to images.

aditya: long term: SDK/CLI changes: 1) session files should be marked `user:interactive` and CLI should refuse to persist interactive sessions into non-interactive environments (CI/containers) unless `--persist-in-container` is specified; 2) add `redwood auth doctor` to detect suspicious session files in repo/image layers.

fran: also a parity issue: some SDKs (go/py) read session file fallback automatically; others require explicit opt-in. we should standardize to require explicit acceptance when reading a session from a container image or read-only filesystem.

sam: telemetry: add `auth.session_embedded_detected` and `auth.container_session_invalidate` events so we can measure prevalence.

docs: will add a short security blurb in quickstart and sample-app README: "If your app runs in containers, ensure you inject credentials at runtime and do not bake session files into images. Use `redwood auth refresh` during deploys."

aditya: tests: add an e2e that simulates a container with baked session and asserts startup warning and auto-invalidation. also add linters for sample repos to fail builds if ~/.redwood/session.json accidentally checked in.

sam: I'll pick up the CLI guard + Dockerfile change. AD will own the linter and docs PR. tagging @eng-devex @platform.

fran: thanks all — oops but glad we caught this before it hit a customer demo :grimacing:
